trajectory.thought: The leader (dba, a seed baseline) has an 'indistinguishable' margin over the runner-up, and the stopping rule says to accept in this case. The series is seasonal-dominated with unstable model rankings and high error correlation, which is exactly the regime where a robust full-pool aggregation like dba excels over fitted weights or narrow subsets. All subset strategies performed worse, confirming that breadth is the right choice here.

action_args.justification: The series is seasonal-dominated (strength 0.60) with weak trend and unstable model rankings (Kendall tau -0.185) across only 3 validation windows. High error correlation (mean 0.926, only 2 independent groups) means narrow subsets add little diversity while losing robustness. The dba (DTW barycenter) over the full 19-model pool is the best strategy and its margin over the runner-up is statistically indistinguishable, so no further refinement is warranted. The full-pool robust aggregation naturally handles the ranking instability and correlated-error redundancy that characterize this series.

- High correlation (0.926) means many models are redundant.
